upload_file: Register a file on a draft (mcp:write).
recid          ... the draft's ID (the id returned by `create_record`)
filename       ... the name to register it under (it becomes the key)
content_base64 ... the content as base64; use this for binaries
content_text   ... the content as plain text; easier for text (encoded as UTF-8)
overwrite      ... replace a file of the same name if one exists (default True).
False reports that it already exists and does nothing.
**Files cannot be added to a published record** (an InvenioRDM rule — make a new
version instead). If the draft has files disabled, they are enabled automatically.
list_files: List a record's files (published records are visible unauthenticated).
draft=True lists the draft's files (requires the owner's authentication).
tools.delete_file: Delete a file from a draft (mcp:write). Files cannot be removed from a published record.
download_file: Retrieve a file's contents (works unauthenticated for published records).
InvenioRDM answers with a **redirect to an S3 presigned URL**. That URL's host is an
in-cluster name (`minio:9000`), so it **cannot be followed from outside the cluster**.
The MCP server therefore fetches it instead and returns the bytes as base64. Anything
that decodes as UTF-8 is also returned in `text`.
draft=True fetches the draft's file (requires the owner's authentication).
new_version: Create a **draft of a new version** of a published record (mcp:write).
InvenioRDM cannot rewrite a published record. To add or replace files you make a new
version, work in it, and publish again.
import_files ... True **carries the previous version's files over**
False starts from a draft with no files.
publication_date ... the new version's publication date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
**InvenioRDM does not carry the publication date into a new version
draft**, so today's date is filled in when this is omitted. Without
version      ... the version label (`v2` and the like). Optional.
The `id` in the result is the new draft's ID. Run `upload_file` and friends against
upload_file_from_url: Hand InvenioRDM a URL and let it fetch the file itself (mcp:write).
`upload_file` carries the bytes as base64, and since MCP responses are JSON that does
not suit large files (default limit 16MB). This tool **only registers a URI**; the
bytes are downloaded asynchronously by InvenioRDM's Celery worker (InvenioRDM
transfer type `F` = FETCH). **There is no size limit.**
**Ordinary users cannot use this on InvenioRDM v14.** The default permission policy
transfer types `L` and `M`; `F` (and `R`) are limited to `SystemProcess()`, meaning
system processes and superusers. Making the server fetch an arbitrary URL is a
potential SSRF, hence the restriction. Without the permission this returns 403.
The target must also be within InvenioRDM's allowed domains
(`RECORDS_RESOURCES_FILES_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`). A URL outside them fails with
**Because it is asynchronous, the fetch may still be running when this returns**
(`status` is `pending`). Confirm completion by checking that `list_files` reports
**A file on your own machine** has no URL and cannot take this path. Use
`start_multipart_upload` for that (no size limit, and ordinary write permission is
start_multipart_upload: **Issue presigned URLs** for sending a large local file (mcp:write).
`upload_file` carries the bytes as base64, so it is bounded by what fits in JSON
(default 16MB). `upload_file_from_url` only works for files that have a URL.
**A large file on your own machine** goes this way (InvenioRDM transfer type
`M` = MULTIPART). The bytes pass through neither the MCP server nor InvenioRDM: they
are PUT **straight from the client to S3 (MinIO)**. There is effectively no size limit.
filename  ... the name to register it under
size      ... the file's **exact byte count** (required; it is declared to S3 up front)
part_size ... bytes per part. Default 64MiB. Every part but the last must be at least
5MiB and all of them the same size
PUT the file to each `url` under `parts` in the result, cutting it into `part_size`
chunks from the beginning. Call `complete_multipart_upload` once every part is sent,
Splitting and sending, as an example (the same text is in `hint` in the result):
complete_multipart_upload: Finalise a multipart upload once every part has been sent (mcp:write).
S3 joins the parts into a single object and the transfer type changes from `M` to `L`
(an ordinary file). **It fails if even one part is missing.**
The `checksum` right afterwards has the form
`multipart:<ETag>-<part count>-<part size>`, which is the composite ETag S3 returns
(the per-part MD5s rolled together). InvenioRDM recomputes the MD5 of the whole file
abort_multipart_upload: Discard a multipart upload that was given up partway (mcp:write).
The incomplete upload on the S3 side is aborted too, so half-sent parts do not linger

client_secret_missing: MCP_SERVER_SECRET is not set. In keycloak mode it has to match the secret configured
on the mcp-server client in Keycloak.
auth.pat_mode_no_exchange: no token exchange in PAT mode (the InvenioRDM personal access token received is used as-is)

errors.auth_mode_invalid: MCP_AUTH_MODE must be keycloak or invenio: {given}
errors.object_store_http: cannot fetch from the object store, HTTP {status}
errors.destructive_needs_confirm: This is a destructive operation. Pass confirm=True.
errors.destructive_effect: the published record becomes a tombstone returning HTTP 410 (restore_record brings it back)
errors.reason_id_invalid: invalid reason_id. Check the valid ids with list_vocabulary('removalreasons')
errors.request_status_invalid: status must be one of {statuses} (there is no open / closed state)
errors.content_exclusive: give exactly one of content_base64 or content_text
errors.upload_too_large: too large: {size} bytes (limit {limit}). MCP arguments are JSON, which does not suit huge files
errors.download_too_large: too large: {size} bytes (limit {limit}). MCP responses are JSON, which does not suit huge files
errors.file_exists: '{filename}' already exists. Pass overwrite=True to replace it
fetch_forbidden: no permission for URL fetching (transfer F). InvenioRDM v14 allows it only to system
Use start_multipart_upload to send a local file instead
errors.import_files_failed: could not carry the files over: {error}
errors.size_must_be_positive: size must be 1 or more (the file's actual byte count)
errors.part_size_too_small: part_size is too small: {part_size}. Every part but the last must be at least {minimum} bytes
errors.no_part_links: no presigned part URLs came back. The storage may not be S3 (local storage uploads go through InvenioRDM instead)

notes.fetch_async: the fetch is asynchronous; it is done once list_files reports status as completed
notes.multipart_hint: split the file with split -b {part_size} <file> part_ and send each piece with curl -X PUT --data-binary @<piece> '<url>'. Once every part is sent, call complete_multipart_upload(recid, filename)
notes.multipart_direct: the bytes go straight to S3 without passing through the MCP server
